existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Fees for copies of records are limited to fees covering the direct costs of duplication, or a statutory fee if one applies.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Except with respect to public records exempt from disclosure by express provisions of law, each state or local agency, upon a request for a copy of records that reasonably describes an identifiable record or records, shall make the records promptly available to any person upon payment of fees covering direct costs of duplication, or a statutory fee if applicable.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Ceiling: the state caps fees at 'direct costs of duplication' (or a separately-authorized statutory fee); the city sets the actual per-copy amount under that ceiling — do not split fixed vs. ceiling into separate concepts. No statewide cents-per-page number exists. Source Type: Statute.

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The cost of duplicating an electronic record is limited to the direct cost of producing a copy of the record in an electronic format.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The cost of duplication of an electronic record pursuant to paragraph (2) of subdivision (b) of Section 7922.570 shall be limited to the direct cost of producing a copy of a record in an electronic format.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Ceiling: city sets the actual electronic-duplication charge under the 'direct cost' cap. Source Type: Statute.

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The requester bears the cost of producing a copy (including the cost to construct a record and the cost of programming and computer services) when the electronic record is produced only at regularly scheduled intervals, or when the request requires data compilation, extraction, or programming to produce the record.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Notwithstanding subdivision (a), the requester shall bear the cost of producing a copy of the record, including the cost to construct a record, and the cost of programming and computer services necessary to produce a copy of the record when either of the following applies: (1) In order to comply with subdivisions (a) and (b) of Section 7922.570, the public agency would be required to produce a copy of an electronic record and the record is one that is produced only at otherwise regularly scheduled intervals. (2) The request would require data compilation, extraction, or programming to produce the record.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Electronic record is produced only at scheduled intervals, OR request requires data compilation/extraction/programming
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: A conditional branch, not a city-set value, so config_home=structural. This is the narrow exception to the direct-cost ceiling in CA-0022. Source Type: Statute.

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: For ordinary production of electronic records, an agency may not charge for the ancillary staff time of searching for and redacting/reviewing records; such time is chargeable only within the narrow data-extraction cost-shift of Section 7922.575(b) (i.e., where extraction/programming or interval-only production applies).
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Under section 6253.9, subdivision (b) [now § 7922.575(b)], the cost of 'data compilation, extraction, or programming' recoverable from a requester does not include the ancillary tasks of searching for, or redacting, otherwise-disclosable electronic records; those tasks must be borne by the agency except in the two circumstances the statute specifies.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_authority: National Lawyers Guild, S.F. Bay Area Chapter v. City of Hayward (2020) 9 Cal.5th 488 (Appellate/Supreme Court Decision)
